text:
alex: FYI — prototyping a 'handshake' ID + richer fallback telemetry for canary rollouts. Need quick feedback before the design review. TL;DR: attach a per-request handshake UUID, emit a short fallback-reason tag, and enforce staged fallback guards: model-variant -> region -> capacity-degrade. Sketch below.

maria: handshake? can you spell out what it buys us vs just tagging fallback reasons?

alex: handshake lets us correlate the canary and control slices for the same logical request sample. if we sample logs/outputs we can compute quality delta even when traffic is split across pools/regions. also helps join traces for latency attribution.

sam: perf overhead? adding header + reason tag per request sounds OK but we should sample. canary volume is already limited.

alex: agreed — sampling config: default sample_rate=5% for telemetry handshake; can bump to 100% for high-risk rollouts. fallback_reason is tiny (enum).

maria: propose the enum values: FallbackModelVariant, FallbackRegionFailover, FallbackCapacityDegrade, FallbackTimeout, FallbackCircuit. that will let us break down root causes in the UI.

alex: yep. example header + response tag:
```
Request headers:
  X-Redwood-Handshake: 8f14e45f-ea9b-4c9c-b1d2-1a2b3c4d5e6f
Response headers:
  X-Redwood-Fallback: FallbackModelVariant;variant=llama2-q4;reason=OOM
  X-Redwood-Trace: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
```

irene: ops perspective: the console needs a small panel: fallback rate by reason, trend, and a histogram of handshake latency. plus an obvious kill-switch to disable automated fallbacks for the rollout.

pm-jordan: we also need to think about user-visible regression: a fallback to a smaller model can change output quality. want to tie fallback automation to a quick-quality-sensor threshold (e.g., golden prompts eval).

alex: proposal for guards:
  - allow-model-variant-fallback only if recent eval delta < 3pt (task-specific metric)
  - region failover allowed only if region error rate > 2x baseline and cross-region probes confirm outage
  - capacity-degrade allowed only if token-estimate veto passes (preflight checks to avoid quota overage)
All of these accompanied by a 'safety score' emitted in telemetry.

sam: token-estimate veto is important — fallback could increase tokens (diff models, longer decoding). ops shouldn't get surprised with usage spikes.

alex: telemetry schema (v1) — short doc snippet:
```json
{
  "handshake_id": "string",
  "sampled": true/false,
  "fallback_reason": "FallbackModelVariant|FallbackRegionFailover|FallbackCapacityDegrade|FallbackTimeout|FallbackCircuit|null",
  "fallback_metadata": "string (kv semicolon-separated)",
  "safety_score": "0-100",
  "canary_bucket": "control|canary",
  "quality_delta": "float|null",
  "token_estimate": "int"
}
```
(note: storing as a compact line-delimited event in the telemetry pipeline)

maria: how do we handle cross-region handshake continuity? UUID must be globally unique and propagated in proxy (edge) + internal router. also join by request id if present.

irene: +1 on manual override. add a per-rollout 'fallback mode' toggle: auto / conservative / manual. conservative only allows non-quality-changing fallbacks (region only?), manual forces ops click.

pm-jordan: metric gating idea: if >X% of golden set fails on control vs canary, automatically pause fallback automation and open an incident.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: model=rwd-llama2-13b-v2, rollout_id=rr-2026-03-18-11, canary_pool=cp-42

sam: small nit — logging format should be stable. use snake_case keys in events and keep fallback_metadata small. also include an abbreviated error code for quick dashboards.

alex: next steps: I'll spin an RFC that includes the header spec, sample rate config, telemetry event schema (compact), and console mock for the fallback panel. tagging @maria @irene @pm-jordan to review before design review next Wed.

irene: sounds good. can you include a short runbook for ops: how to pause/unpause and manual remediation steps?

alex: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
